method: Jaccard token ranking of actual visible stem+all choices; scores are discovery only

visible_originals.stem:
A 39-year-old patient presents for an otherwise eligible non-vaccine medication under DCP 26-03-124. The proposed route is IM; the product is in single-dose packaging. A valid prescription has not been issued. A trained pharmacist with current CPR would administer it, with appropriate supervision for an intern. All other product-specific requirements are satisfied.

Which assessment best addresses the stated limiting condition? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Proceed under this pathway if all stated product and supervision conditions remain satisfied.
Do not use this circular as the authority for this patient’s age.
Resolve the stated prescription or professional-role defect before administration.
Change or clarify the route/packaging plan before relying on this circular.

visible_originals.stem:
A 22-year-old patient presents for an otherwise eligible non-vaccine medication under DCP 26-03-124. The proposed route is IM; the product is in single-dose packaging. A valid prescription is on file. A trained certified technician with current CPR would administer it, with appropriate supervision for an intern. All other product-specific requirements are satisfied.

Which assessment best addresses the stated limiting condition? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Change or clarify the route/packaging plan before relying on this circular.
Proceed under this pathway if all stated product and supervision conditions remain satisfied.
Resolve the stated prescription or professional-role defect before administration.
Do not use this circular as the authority for this patient’s age.

visible_originals.stem:
A Massachusetts retail pharmacy offers medication administration under DCP 26-03-124. The cases do not involve a hospital privilege or a separately authorized opioid treatment program. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A trained pharmacist with current CPR administers an eligible single-dose LAI to an adult under a valid prescription and product requirements.
A qualified intern administers an eligible adult patient’s IM medication under appropriate pharmacist supervision.
A pharmacist immediately informs the prescriber after an administration reaction requiring emergency-department monitoring.
A pharmacy documents patient consent, screening, lot, expiry, administration route/site, and administering professional.
A pharmacy administers ceftriaxone intravenously using the circular’s IM authorization.

visible_originals.stem:
Case A: A technician qualified to vaccinate is assigned to administer a long-acting injectable antipsychotic under the general medication-administration circular.

Case B: A pharmacist proposes using that circular to administer an otherwise eligible medication intravenously to a 17-year-old.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Vaccination qualification does not place the technician within this pharmacist-or-intern medication pathway.
The limited individual MCSR exception for administration does not waive all pharmacy facility registrations.
The proposed intravenous administration to a 17-year-old does not meet this pathway's age and route conditions.
An eligible medication must also meet the specified single-dose packaging and prescription conditions.

visible_originals.stem:
Case A: After an eligible medication injection, the patient requires additional treatment and monitoring in an emergency department; staff plan to wait 24 hours before notifying the prescriber.

Case B: A nonserious reaction in another patient is discussed under the circular's recommendation for communication within 24 hours.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A prescriber call does not replace a separately triggered Board report for an error or serious event.
The serious outcome requires immediate prescriber notification rather than waiting for the routine interval.
Emergency care must not be delayed while staff finish the report.
The ordinary 24-hour communication wording is a recommendation distinct from the immediate mandatory category.

visible_originals.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist chooses the statewide emergency-contraception standing-order pathway but assumes an additional training course is a mandatory entry condition under that pathway.

Case B: An agent requests a standing-order prescription for someone who will take the medication, but the pharmacist has not contacted or assessed that person.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Participation in this service is voluntary, while independently applicable dispensing-access duties remain.
The described statewide EC pathway does not impose the additional mandatory training assumed in the first case.
The standing order is a specific authority rather than a general independent prescribing license.
The actual intended user must be assessed through the allowed in-person or telephone pathway.

visible_originals.stem: A pharmacist discovers that an improper warfarin dispensing caused a patient to be hospitalized, and the facts meet the serious-injury reporting criteria in 247 CMR 20.02(1). Which statements correctly distinguish the duties triggered by this same event? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist’s initial QRE documentation remains subject to the 24-hour discovery-or-notification clock.
The seven-business-day Board reporting period is measured from the date the prescription was originally written.
The manager of record must report the qualifying improper dispensing within seven business days of discovery of the related serious injury or death.
Completing the QRE record eliminates the separate serious-event report because both rules concern the same dispensing error.
The event can trigger both CQI documentation and the separate serious-event reporting pathway because the rules have different purposes and clocks.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed the required administration training and maintains current CPR certification. Each option involves a medication that appears on the MH/SUD administration list. Which requests may proceed under the current guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A 34-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Vivitrol supplied in its single-dose presentation
A 45-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for Invega Sustenna, but this would be the patient's first dose of the medication
A 39-year-old patient requests Abilify Maintena from anonymous pharmacy floor stock that is not tied to a patient-specific prescribed single dose
A 17-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Invega Sustenna
A 52-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Abilify Maintena supplied as the prescribed single dose

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist administers a patient-specific dose of Abilify Maintena under the mental-illness administration pathway. Shortly afterward, the patient develops a severe reaction requiring emergency medical services and evaluation in an emergency department. Which follow-through actions are consistent with current Massachusetts guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Immediately report the adverse event to the prescriber because emergency-department treatment is one of the specified serious outcomes
Record the adverse outcome or adverse event in the pharmacy's administration record
If the event is a dispensing error or a serious adverse drug event, fulfill the pharmacist's or intern's applicable Board reporting responsibility
Delay prescriber communication until the next routine reassessment because the patient has already been transferred to emergency care
Omit the event from the pharmacy record when emergency medical services create their own clinical documentation

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacist is asked to begin collaboratively managing a walk-in who says her physician mentioned that the pharmacy could help with her blood pressure. Nothing is in writing and the pharmacist has had no contact with the physician. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: She is a collaborative patient because her own physician suggested it.
She is a collaborative patient because she has presented herself for the service.
The supervising physician must assess her and include a diagnosis on referral.
She becomes a collaborative patient once the pharmacist records the conversation.
In this setting she must be notified of and must consent to the services.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist faces a medical emergency at 2 a.m. The only prescription on hand is marked 'no substitution', the prescribed brand is not in stock, and an interchangeable product on the Massachusetts list is. The pharmacist dispenses the interchangeable product. Which statements about this dispensing are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A medical emergency permits filling a 'no substitution' prescription this way when the brand is out of stock.
The pharmacist's own note of the emergency completes what the regulation asks of the pharmacy.
The date, hour and nature of the emergency must be recorded on the prescription or in the pharmacy system.
The purchaser must indicate acceptance of the deviation in writing.
The deviation runs only toward the cheaper product, never toward the brand as written.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed manufacturer injection training and has safely used the same device in another licensed role. The pharmacy now asks the pharmacist to administer a prescription product that is not on the Department's current eligible-medication list and does not fall within another recognized Massachusetts pharmacist-administration pathway. Which conclusions are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Device training may support personal competence, but it does not add the product to the legally recognized administration scope.
Demonstrated technical skill alone authorizes administration of any prescription injectable.
The pharmacist must satisfy both the individual education, training, and experience standard and the applicable legal scope for the product and act.
Placement of the product on the pharmacy's internal protocol is equivalent to inclusion in the Department's eligible-medication guidance.
On these facts, the pharmacist should not administer the product solely on the strength of prior device experience.

visible_originals.stem:
An adult asks for a patient-specific emergency-contraception prescription for a friend under the Massachusetts statewide standing-order pathway. The pharmacist has not spoken with the person who will use the medicine.

Which next step fits that pathway? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Use the purchaser's history as the intended patient's screening record.
Generate the prescription under the purchaser's name and change it after pickup.
Contact and assess the intended patient, using an allowed phone or in-person route.
Require the intended patient to be physically present even if a telephone assessment is available.
